known_issues.status: RESOLVED — fixed and committed as 0b88600 in prometheus-entity-sync
known_issues.description: ConnectionHandler::poll_deltas stored the last-delivered LSN (inclusive) and reused it directly as BucketOpLog::drain_since's scan start — but drain_since is also inclusive of from_lsn, so every ~50ms poll tick re-included the already-delivered op, forever. Shipped in the already-archived, already-security-reviewed v4-pes-gateway change; only caught now because v4-entity-sync-ts-sdk's Docker integration tests were the first coverage to run the delta loop for more than a few assertions and check delivery *count*, not just presence. Fixed by scanning from last_seen_lsn + 1 (kept local to the scan, distinct from the inclusive-by-contract last_seen_lsn field). Regression test: crates/pes-gateway/tests/e2e_delta_propagation.rs's a_single_write_is_delivered_as_exactly_one_delta_not_repeated.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED — fixed and committed as 0b88600 in prometheus-entity-sync
known_issues.description: resume_lsn: Some(PgLsn(0)) was used in several Rust E2E tests and in entity-sync-core's SyncClient.subscribe(buckets, "0") calls as a shortcut to skip snapshot delivery. This is ambiguous: PgLsn(0) is a real, reachable value (WalToBucketRouter's broker-Offset surrogate LSN starts at 0), so Some(0) cannot be distinguished from 'I've already consumed the op at LSN 0.' Once the redelivery bug above was fixed, poll_deltas correctly started treating Some(0) as already-consumed, which silently dropped each client's first op. User decided (via AskUserQuestion) to fix the affected tests to use the real resume_lsn: None + snapshot-then-live-delta path rather than introduce a distinct sentinel type. e2e_write_authorization.rs and e2e_graceful_shutdown.rs keep Some(0) — audited and confirmed safe since neither asserts on Delta receipt.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED — fixed and committed as 0b88600 in prometheus-entity-sync
known_issues.description: entity-sync-core's Docker integration tests called SyncClient.subscribe() and then immediately wrote to Postgres via a direct pool.query, with no wait for the WebSocket connection to actually reach the server and process Subscribe. If the write committed first, the entity landed in the (already-in-flight) snapshot instead of arriving as a Delta, and tests that only listened via onDelta would hang until timeout. Fixed by adding a trackStatus()/waitForLive() helper that waits for SyncClient's onStatus callback to report state: "live" before writing, used in the two-tab bidirectional sync and offline/reconnect tests (the JWT refresh test already had an 8s wait for unrelated reasons and wasn't affected).
known_issues.verified_by: diagnosed both this race and the LSN-0/redelivery bugs above via a hand-rolled Node script that spoke the raw WebSocket+MessagePack protocol directly against the running docker-compose server, bypassing SyncClient entirely, to confirm the fixed pes-gateway delivers exactly one Delta per write before touching any TS-side code.

known_issues.description: This dev environment uses Colima, not Docker Desktop. testcontainers' bollard client defaults to /var/run/docker.sock and ignores `docker context`; set DOCKER_HOST=unix:///Users/gqadonis/.colima/default/docker.sock when running any testcontainers-backed test locally. Not needed in CI with a standard Docker socket.

frf-postgres-cdc's WAL decoder hard-requires every watched table's id column to be UUID-parseable; a non-UUID id silently drops the row with only a WARN log. Real schemas synced through this system need UUID primary keys on any CDC-watched table.

No tsconfig.json existed anywhere in the repo until v4-psync-protocol needed real TS type-checking. Added a root tsconfig.json plus one for entity-sync-core; all 4 TS packages typecheck clean now. Other TS packages (entity-sync-pglite, entity-sync-react, entity-sync-tauri) don't yet have their own package-level tsconfig.json — add one when each gains real content, following entity-sync-core's pattern.

pes_rules::template::substitute rendered {bucket_parameters.X} unquoted, producing invalid SQL for any non-numeric owner column (e.g. UUID) since Postgres parses an unquoted UUID literal as an arithmetic expression. Found writing pes-gateway's first E2E test — no prior test suite exercised the real substitution path against Postgres with a non-numeric column. Fix renders values as single-quoted SQL string literals; docs/sync-rules-reference.md updated to document the new convention.

pes-snapshot's keyset pagination failed with 'operator does not exist: uuid > text' for any UUID-keyed table: the IdCast::Text branch cast only the cursor bind, not the id column itself, so Postgres compared a native uuid against text with no valid operator. Found the same way as the pes-rules bug above — no prior pes-snapshot test used a non-numeric id column.

known_issues.status: design note, not a bug — followed the written proposal, flagged for future consideration
known_issues.description: v4-pem-sync-transport's proposal specifies wiring prometheus-entity-sync into PEM via EntityTransport<T> (entity-graph-core's pull-based list/get/subscribe contract, same one makeRestTransport implements). But prometheus-entity-management/packages/entity-graph-sync already has a purpose-built SyncProvider interface (start/pushLocalChange/stop) specifically for realtime CRDT peer sync, with Yjs/Loro providers already implemented there — architecturally a closer fit for a persistent WebSocket delta stream than EntityTransport's request/response shape. User confirmed following the proposal exactly (EntityTransport<T>) rather than redirecting to SyncProvider, to keep this change on-spec and contained. Worth a future design discussion on whether entity-graph-sync should also get a prometheus-entity-sync SyncProvider — would let CRDT-heavy consumers use the more purpose-built path.

Both examples/vite-app and examples/nextjs-app's task-hooks.ts (for the Task entity) still use the 1.x useEntityList/useEntity hooks with inline fetch: closures reading from a mock backend, not the 2.0 useEntities/useEntityQuery + registerEntityTransport pattern. This predates (or wasn't migrated during) the v3.0.0 monorepo restructure. v4-pem-sync-transport's new src/lib/entity-sync-transport.ts in each app demonstrates the registration API compiles and typechecks correctly, but is not actually wired into either app's rendered Task views. A future change would need to migrate task-hooks.ts to the 2.0 pattern to make prometheusSyncTransport's data actually reach the UI.

known_issues.status: RESOLVED — fixed and committed as 1ab1d99 (MEDIUM finding from pre-commit security review)
known_issues.description: pes-server's config.toml env-var interpolation (${VAR_NAME}) did raw text substitution into the TOML source before parsing — an env var value containing a quote followed by TOML syntax could break out of its string literal and inject arbitrary config structure. Fixed by escaping interpolated values per TOML basic-string escape rules before splicing them in. Regression test: crates/pes-server/src/config.rs's env_var_value_cannot_break_out_of_its_toml_string_literal.
